title: Closest Divisors
description:
Given an integer num, find the closest two integers in absolute difference whose product equals num + 1 or num + 2.
Return the two integers in any order.
 
Example 1:

Input: num = 8
Output: [3,3]
Explanation: For num + 1 = 9, the closest divisors are 3 & 3, for num + 2 = 10, the closest divisors are 2 & 5, hence 3 & 3 is chosen.

Example 2:

Input: num = 123
Output: [5,25]

Example 3:

Input: num = 999
Output: [40,25]

 
Constraints:

1 <= num <= 10^9

check_function:
def check(candidate):
    assert sorted(candidate(num = 8)) == [3, 3]
    assert sorted(candidate(num = 123)) == [5, 25]
    assert sorted(candidate(num = 999)) == [25, 40]
    assert sorted(candidate(num = 1)) == [1, 2]
    assert sorted(candidate(num = 2)) == [2, 2]
    assert sorted(candidate(num = 10)) == [3, 4]
    assert sorted(candidate(num = 25)) == [3, 9]
    assert sorted(candidate(num = 100)) == [6, 17]
    assert sorted(candidate(num = 999999)) == [1000, 1000]
